Join us as part of the Lunar New Year Festival 2026 for a delicious cultural experience!
✨ What We’ll Make Together:
🍃 Bánh Tét / Bánh Chưng – iconic sticky rice cakes wrapped in banana leaves, symbolising family reunion and prosperity
🥒 Dưa Món (Pickled Vegetables) – crunchy, colourful pickles that balance the richness of New Year dishes
🍖 Thịt Kho (Caramelized Braised Pork) – tender pork simmered in coconut water, a dish that brings comfort, warmth and the taste of Tết
This workshop is designed for all ages — beginners, families, food lovers, and anyone curious about Vietnamese culture. Learn the meaning behind each dish and how they come together on every Vietnamese New Year table.
💛 Why Join?
• Experience authentic Vietnamese Tết traditions
• Learn recipes passed down through generations
• Connect with community through shared stories and food
• Take home what you cook
• Celebrate culture in a warm, hands-on environment

description:
Cheesemaking - Brie And Queso Fresco, During this intensely practical, hands-on workshop, you will be guided through each step of the cheesemaking process while making your very own round of Double Cream ‘NZ style’ Brie. You will also be shown how to make Queso Fresco cheese which you will get to sample afterwards. All ingredients included in course fee.

The ultimate class in practical cheese making! Learn all you need to know to replicate making NZ style Brie and Queso Fresco at home. You will be guided through each step of the cheesemaking process while making your very own round of Brie. Then, while the Brie is ripening and setting (don't worry, all terminology will be explained!), we will make Queso Fresco together.

All ingredients are provided as are recipes and detailed handouts to take away with you. Bring an apron, a dishcloth, 3 or 4 tea towels, a pen to take notes and a 2 litre container and plastic re-sealable food bags to take your cheese home.

During the workshop, the following topics will also be covered: Milk and where to source it, hygiene and sanitation, equipment required and the origins of the cheeses you are about to make. You will also receive comprehensive instruction on how to mature your Brie cheese over the next few weeks.

A small break will be provided and you will have the opportunity to purchase equipment and cheesemaking ingredients after the workshop should you wish to replicate the experience at home.

By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:
- Make Brie and Queso Fresco
- Recall the best milk to use and where to source it from
- Name and identify what equipment and ingredients you need to make Brie and Queso Fresco

Note: Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

1 Day
Presented by Alexis Murti.

What's so simple about simple syrup? Who was Count Negroni? And what's so old fashioned about the Old Fashioned anyway? We'll talk about all of this and more all while tantalising those tastebuds with a little mixology.

In some cases, you will also be able to sample variations of drinks that we will demo so you can see how different techniques affect what happens in the glass. description:
Vietnamese Pâté Chaud (Bánh Pa-tê Sô), Join Viet Hub NZ for a free Vietnamese cooking workshop celebrating one of Vietnam’s most-loved pastries — Bánh Pa-tê Sô (Vietnamese Pâté Chaud).
In this relaxed, hands-on session, you’ll learn how this golden, flaky pastry is made, explore its key flavours, and hear the cultural stories behind a snack many Vietnamese families grew up with. The workshop is beginner-friendly and designed as a welcoming space to cook, taste, and connect through food.
What makes this workshop special is not just the recipe, but the sharing of culture, memory, and community. Whether you’re new to Vietnamese cuisine or reconnecting with familiar flavours, you’ll leave with new knowledge, warm food, and a deeper appreciation of Vietnamese food culture.
Free to attend | All ingredients provided | Limited spaces – registration required
Come cook with us, meet new people, and enjoy a meaningful cultural experience through food.
This workshop is proudly delivered by Viet Hub NZ, in collaboration with Te Tai Ohinga | Central City Youth Hub, supporting accessible, inclusive spaces for cultural learning and connection ❤️.

description:
Tītahi Bay Spring Community BBQ, Tītahi Bay Spring Community BBQ
It's (nearly) summer so it's time for a BBQ! Come and join us at 43 Kapiti Crescent (St Matthew's Hall) for a BBQ on the lawn. If it's bad weather, we will move into the hall.

All welcome! Dinner will be served from 5pm; we will make dinner, so just bring yourselves!



FAQ

Who is this for? Can I come along?

Yes absolutely, please come, we would love to have you. This dinner is for all the people who live in the beautiful community of Tītahi Bay!

What if I can't make it until a bit later?

That's all good, we will be serving a rolling dinner from 5 to 6.30pm so come whenever suits you. If you can only come a little later than 6.30pm, we will likely have more than enough so come anyway!

Can I bring my kids along?

Yes! In fact, please bring your kids along. We will have some games in the room and some options for crafts on the tables along with the food.

Do I need to bring anything?

Nope! Just yourselves, all are welcome just as you are.

But I really want to bring something to contribute?

If you would like to bring a salad to contribute to the BBQ, feel free to email us at and we can chat! We really just don't want this to be a barrier to anyone coming along.

Can I help?

Yes absolutely, this is a community event so help is always appreciated. It is also a great time to meet some other people. We will have some tasks for set up and also some for packing down and cleaning up. If you are interested in helping, flick us an email at

Will my dietaries be met?

We will make sure there will be options for these dietaries: vegan, gluten free, dairy free, and nut free.

If you have a dietary that isn't on there, feel free to check and flick us an email.

Can I bring my friend(s) along?

description:
Belmont Historic Bunker walk, Step into history and explore Belmont’s WWII munitions bunkers at Belmont Regional Park.

Join us for a unique opportunity to explore Aotearoa New Zealand’s WWII history at Belmont Regional Park.

Built in 1943, the Belmont Munitions Depot was once the country’s largest ammunition storage site, chosen for its strategic location near shipping routes and Trentham Military Camp, and its safe distance from populated areas. The depot originally held 62 magazines storing anti-aircraft shells, mortar rounds, grenades, and other munitions—including 1,500 tonnes of mustard gas, believed to be the largest store of chemical weapons in New Zealand.

This self-led, easy 2.5 km circuit walk follows the well-known Magazine Mile, winding through open farmland with expansive park views. Along the route, historians will be on-site to share stories and insights into Belmont’s vital role in supporting New Zealand and U.S. troops in the Pacific during World War II.

Walk at your own pace as you explore historic bunkers, uncover wartime secrets, and discover how this quiet landscape helped shape the Pacific war effort.

Time: 10.00am – 1.00pm
Meeting point: Belmont Regional Park, Hill Road entrance

Please note this event is limited to 60 car parks, so we encourage people to carpool where possible. To help us manage car park capacity, each registration is for ONE vehicle only (if you wish to register for more than one vehicle, please complete additional registrations)

description:
Visit the Upper Hutt Blockhouse, Visit the Upper Hutt Blockhouse
This Heritage New Zealand Pouhere Taonga property is not open to the public often, so bring the family between 11am and 1pm.

Visit Upper Hutt Blockhouse as part of the Wellington Heritage Festival 2025.

The Upper Hutt Blockhouse is one of the few remaining buildings associated with the New Zealand Wars, as well as a monument to Pākehā settler anxiety, built in fear of an attack by Māori that never came.

Visit today and you’ll get a sense of the defensive ‘last stand’ mindset. On both floors you’ll find a series of balistraria, tightly angled gun slots through which members of the militia would defend their posts.

Keep an eye out, too, for an exposed panel where you can see the fine gravel that was packed between the exterior weatherboards and inch-thick interior boards to absorb the impact of answering gunfire. Don’t be fooled by the windows – they were added later. Originally, the loop holes you’ll spy on the walls were the only way to see out.

Inside the Blockhouse, there’s an exhibition from Whirinaki Whare Taonga, telling the early story of Upper Hutt and its Blockhouse.

We will have some knowledgeable people available to share stories, answer questions and some light refreshments. Drop in between 11-1pm and stay as long as you like!


Booking is REQUIRED.
Cost: $10 - $15
Booking information here: https://wellingtonheritagefestival.co.nz/event/visit-the-upper-hutt-blockhouse/

description:
ANZAC Day - 2026 Open Day, NEWS RELEASE :
FOR IMMEDIATE USE - April 2026
ANZAC DAY - OPEN DAY- SATURDAY 25th April: 10AM - 4PM.
Wellington’s historic Wrights Hill Fortress in Karori is open for public inspection again on ANZAC Day, SATURDAY, April 25th. The World War Two coastal battery first opened to the public in 1989 and will be accessible between 10am - 4pm.
On ANZAC Day people are invited to self-guide themselves through the tunnels and gun emplacements. The walk usually takes about one hour. Bring a torch with you for some fun!
Visitors will be able to explore the 620 metres of underground tunnels with a free map and history pamphlet. They will see the engine room, shell stores, plotting rooms and the huge gun pit where Gun Number 1 used to stand, as well as a replica of the 10-metre-long gun barrel.
Also on show will be historic photos, and a DVD of how a 9.2-inch gun operates will be showing as well. The World War Two Fortress will also have period themed displays. It’s only open to the public on four Open Days a year.
Wrights Hill Fortress was built from 1942 to protect Wellington from Japanese bombardment. In the early 1960’s, the guns were cut up for scrap and sold, ironically, to the Japanese.
Admission is $20 for a family of two adults and three children under 15, or $10 per adult and $5 per child. (Sorry no EFTPOS -CASH ONLY) Access is via Karori Road, Campbell Street, and Wrights Hill Road. All proceeds go to the continuing restoration of the Fortress. There is limited car parking at the summit of Wrights Hill. Please Park sensibly and use walking tracks.
Visitors to the Fortress in Wrights Hill Reserve can also enjoy picnic sites and panoramic views from the top of the hill. There will be a BBQ sausage sizzle and soft drinks on sale. For safety reasons no jandals please.

description:
January Full Moon Drumming, January Full Moon Drumming
Please remember this is a ZERO WASTE and *NO ALCOHOL* community gathering.
Kia ora!
Full Moon Drumming Wellington is a registered public event with the Wellington City Council. We are a group of humans from all walks of life who gather under the full moon each month to connect through drumming and dance around the fire. This gathering is participatory, that means if you made it to the circle you are part of the circle. As in Africa, there is no audience! Everyone is invited to participate as part of the ‘chorus’ (singing/clapping), dancing, or drumming.
The event is weather permitting, we check the forecast a few days prior and aim to make a decision the day before the event, although this is not possible and sometimes we make the decision on the day. All updates are posted on the event page.
This gathering is entirely run by volunteers, if you'd like to contribute in any way please get in touch.
There are a few things that we need help with:
- FIREWOOD: Please bring dry firewood as a koha, no wood no fire! Please NOTE we DO NOT burn pallets (due to nails) or treated timber. Feel free to post or reach out if you have a vehicle and are keen to help gather firewood on the day of the event.
- BEAUTIFYING THE CIRCLE SPACE: Anyone has fairy lights, oil burners, or is keen to make some signs?
NOTE: We hold a fire permit for this event. For safety reasons we don't allow participants to feed the fire, and while is generally okay to roast some marshmallows early in the evening we don't allow the use the fire for cooking or heating food.
This is an **ALCOHOL FREE EVENT**, please help us uphold this kaupapa and remind those who are unaware and might be new to the event that alcohol is not permitted. As hosts we are responsible for your safety and we take that responsibility seriously, especially given that the event is authorised through both fire and event permits. Large, public, all ages gatherings require administration and logistics so please respect this and the guidelines provided.
Princess Bay is within Taputeranga Marine Reserve ( https://octopus.org.nz/taputeranga-marine-reserve), we are welcomed to gather each month in this special place so let’s all make sure there is NO RUBBISH LEFT BEHIND and that we take care of the space. Dogs are NOT ALLOWED at the gathering - there are Korora (Blue Pinguins) nesting under the rocks nearby and we've had issues with dogs in the past.
Children are welcome at the fire, though, especially after dark, please make sure that all children have adult supervision, that the supervisors are aware of the children they are looking after, and that the children are aware of who is looking after them.
Feel free to bring:
- Your friends.
- Drums or any percussive instrument.
- Warm clothing; jackets and wool blankets are good.
- Something to seat on (otherwise sand is often wet)
- Drinking water.
- Food, tea to share.
- Your lovely selves.
- Fire spinning kit and fuel.
FIRE SPINNERS: Please take all precautionary safety measures and make sure to set up fire-spinning downwind from the fire circle.
PARKING: There's a parking lot a few hundred meters from the fire circle where there's also public toilets. Please also be aware of our neighbors driveway opposite the stairway and do not park directly in front of it.
CARPOOLING: If you don't have a way to get to Princess Bay, or if you have spare seats in your car, feel free to post it on the event page. The less cars driving the better.
Feel free to share the event page and send an event invite to whomever you feel would be interested, not everyone sees the notifications and advertising

GROUNDWORK: an author talk with Michele Leggott and Catherine Field-Dodgson, Join us to hear authors Michele Leggott and Catherine Field-Dodgson discuss Emily Cumming Harris, the subject of their book 'Groundwork', and one of Aotearoa's most significant female artists of the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries.
Just as Emily Harris’s beautiful paintings occupy a liminal space between scientific botanical illustration and art, so this book occupies a shifting ground between biography and imagineered monograph. The result is often moving and always intriguing. Importantly, it restores to Aotearoa art history a figure who had almost disappeared.
Emily Harris has been examined alongside her artist peers Sarah Featon and Georgina Hetley, but until this book neither her distinctive voice nor her almost 200 surviving images have been heard or seen in any quantity outside of archival or online spaces.
Her life story is remarkable and her diaries, letters, poems and paintings constitute a fascinating legacy. In 'Groundwork', with its compelling text, they are lovingly brought together for the first time.
Michele and Catherine will be bringing copies of Emily's hand-coloured book 'New Zealand Flowers, Berries and Ferns' to display.

Guitarist, singer and songwriter Bill Lake is a cornerstone of Aotearoa’s musical landscape. With a career spanning more than four decades, Bill has shaped the sound of New Zealand roots music—leading the iconic Windy City Strugglers, co-founding the pioneering rock outfit Mammal, and fronting the brassy, groove-laden Pelicans in the 80s.
A gifted storyteller with a wry lyrical touch, Bill’s songs have been covered by Midge Marsden, Darren Watson, Kokomo, Rag Poets and Marg Layton. His live performances are intimate, soulful affairs—equal parts reflection and revelation.
Bill is joined by longtime friend and Mammal bandmate Steve Hemmens, recently returned from the UK, whose supple bass lines bring warmth and swing. Rounding out the trio is multi-instrumentalist Alan Norman (The Warratahs, Rag Poets), adding colour and texture on accordion, percussion, guitar and piano.
Together, they offer a rich, rootsy blend of blues, folk and country—music with heart, history, and a touch of Wellington grit.

Fat Freddy’s Drop, Doing it for the love of music, Fat Freddy’s Drop takes to the Michael Fowler Centre stage in May 2026. They’ll be there for three nights performing their ground-breaking debut album, ‘Based On A True Story’. The tour will mark the first live performances since the sudden death of founding band member Chris ‘MU’ Faiumu.
Lead singer Dallas Tamaira says, “It’s important for us to honour the intentions we had with MU and playing this album live is part of that.” ‘Based On A True Story’ was independently released in 2005. It became Aotearoa’s longest-charting album with 111 weeks in the Top 40. It also won eight NZ Music Awards and took out Giles Peterson’s Worldwide Music Awards in the UK.
Twenty years later, the band’s unique funk and roots style has become a defining sound of Aotearoa. “[Based On A True Story] was the band’s first full-length studio album, and its success was the springboard for what has been an incredible journey together,” explains saxophonist Scott Towers. “We want to pay tribute to the music, to MU, and the band he established. And, of course, to play to our fans around the world who have supported us through everything.”

Sydney-born pianist and educator Tony Lee has gained a reputation as one of Australia's finest young pianists. He seeks to transmit the essence of music and his understanding of it through his performances and teaching. Tony was an artist in residence at the Chapelle Musicale Reine Elisabeth in Belgium and worked closely with the renowned Portuguese Swiss pianist Maria-João Pires between 2014-2019.

In 2023, Tony served on the Piano Faculty at the Zhejiang Normal University and Emporia State University Undergraduate Joint Program and now holds the position of Artistic Advisor for the Rising Stars Program at the Sydney Conservatorium of Music.

Tony has performed across the Asia Pacific, Europe, the USA and has appeared as soloist with the BBC Philharmonic Orchestra, Brussels Philharmonic Orchestra, National Ballet of China Symphony Orchestra, Shanghai Philharmonic Orchestra, Lanzhou Symphony Orchestra, Chengdu Philharmonic Orchestra, Guangxi Symphony Orchestra, Samara Philharmonic Orchestra, Queensland Symphony Orchestra, Adelaide Symphony Orchestra, Tasmanian Symphony Orchestra, and New Zealand Symphony Orchestra.

An intuitive art project born from raw passion;

and enactment. Whilst wielding a lyrical and musical
medium largely inspired by – and seeking to
channel – the primeval essence of the human experience,
flashes of illumination will descend the sky
from which there shall be no shelter.
Forged of an intense understanding between drummer
Fabian Wyrsch and guitarist Okoi Jones, the
project first took physical form in 2008. Before
long, the dualistic significance of their musical partnership
outshone any need for a bass player and
has since served to both challenge and empower the
band’s creativity. Following their 2010 live debut in

conjuring up mighty barriers of sound with nothing
but a ten-stringed guitar and an almost ritualistic
percussion style. The pair describe their own stage
experience as a form of spiritual rapture, an atavistic
vortex woven together from the profound union
of spectacle meeting spectator on a deeper plane.

MINUIT : The Reunion Shows | PŌNEKE (Wellington), SOLD OUT!!!!
After over a decade away, legendary NZ electronic act Minuit are back – and bringing their iconic live show to Wellington.
..................................................................................................
This reunion makes us very happy because we thought it might never happen – ‘the Kiwi band with the French name’ are back together for a series of shows.
Singer, Ruth, describes the gigs as: "a chance to dance, laugh and sing (in my case, often the wrong words), together live one more time."
Minuit (minwee) became a must-see live act through the 2000s. Fronted by the enigmatic Ruth Carr, her coy persona ignites while bandmates Ryan Beehre and Paul Dodge forge rib-rattling beats around her.
Their debut album, The 88, released in 2003, achieved gold status in New Zealand, quickly followed up by the 'I Hate Guns' EP.
Over the following decade, the trio toured their synths and samplers from Helsinki to Hanoi crafting their own refreshing sound – storming The Crystal Method's club night in LA, the FabricLive birthday bash in London, and headlining the Hanoi Music Festival in Vietnam. Along with festivals and shows up and down Aotearoa.
Having been retired since 2014, we’re excited to announce that Minuit are back onstage for a limited number of reunion shows.
These reunion performances will pay tribute to classic tunes from all four albums 'The Boy with the Aubergine Hair', 'Except You', 'Fuji', 'Menace', ‘Aotearoa’, ‘I Hate Guns’, ‘A Room Full of Cute’, 'Last Night You Saw This Band', ‘25 Bucks’ – everything gets a look in, plus a couple of other surprises.

description:
Vera Ellen - Heave Knows What Time, Vera Ellen - Heave Knows What Time
Aotearoa Music Award-winning and Taite Award-winning artist Vera Ellen releases her new album Heaven Knows What Time. on May 1 via Flying Nun Records. Alongside the album release, Vera Ellen returns to Aotearoa in July for a six-date national tour in celebration of Heaven Knows What Time.

The title Heaven Knows What Time. arrived while Vera was lying on the top bunk of a house truck in Buenos Aires, nearly two years after writing the record and almost a year after completing the mix. After multiple working titles, it surfaced with clarity and immediacy - less a decision than a moment of recognition. It reflects the album’s central tension: frustration and surrender to forces outside of control. As Vera describes it, creativity cannot be demanded - it can be nurtured, but ultimately arrives in its own time, “like a baby”.

The album was written during a two-week songwriting residency in Greytown, awarded through the NZ Pacific Studio Artist Residency Programme. The residency provided space and solitude away from touring and performance, culminating in a performance at Studio 73 for fellow residents and members of the local community.
‍

In her residency application, Vera wrote: “After the heaviness of Ideal Home Noise, I feel it is pressing that I now create an uplifting record that has a guiding message of hope, but from a matured perspective.” While that intention is present, Heaven Knows What Time. resists neat resolution, moving through themes of love, joy, self-assurance, humour, moodiness, and heartbreak - positioning Vera as an observer of both inner and outer worlds.

Alongside extensive touring in Aotearoa — including the 2025 Laneway Festival — Vera has performed internationally with her band, including a 14-date tour of China, a sold-out run in Australia supporting Crowded House, appearances at New Colossus Festival and SXSW (Austin and Sydney), and a full UK/EU support tour with Yumi Zouma. She is set to support Aldous Harding on her full UK/EU tour and perform at The Great Escape in Brighton. The Guardian described her performance as: “Arising New Zealand empress Vera Ellen and band were a revelation, a shimmering reminder that pop’n’roll can still nudge one’s soul.”

description:
Nonconnah (USA) / 1/3 Octave Band, Nonconnah is an experimental music collective based in Memphis, Tennessee, headed by the husband-and-wife duo of Zachary Corsa and Denny Wilkerson Corsa.
Nonconnah creates haunting soundscapes and collages, often using antique or unusual instrumentation and obsolete recording technology to draw on themes of memory and the past, the supernatural, and the liminal spaces where the man-made and natural worlds meet.
Releases such as 2021's Songs for and About Ghosts are filled with warped lo-fi guitars, field recordings, grainy samples, and acoustic instrumentation, arranged into dreamlike sequences. The Corsas draw on a wide range of sonic influences, from shoegaze and post-rock to dark ambient to recurring motifs of old time/Appalachian mountain music.
A highly collaborative effort, Nonconnah has collaborated with past and present members of bands like Deerhoof, Swans, Earth, Broken Social Scene, Arcade Fire, A Silver Mt. Zion and many more.

Stephen Gallagher is an Emmy award-winning composer and music editor who has worked on an extensive range of projects, from global blockbusters to television and contemporary dance. Most recently, he completed the score for The Lord of the Rings: The War of the Rohirrim, directed by Kenji Kamiyama. Gallagher's work spans collaborations with Peter Jackson, Brian Eno, Ed Sheeran, Nick Cave, and many more.
David Long is a composer, performer, founding member of The Mutton Birds, and member of easy listening noise band, Teeth. His career has spanned over 40 years and seen him work on numerous projects to commercial and critical acclaim. In his own words he likes to "mash shit up", creating orchestral scores that utilise "not only classical instruments but all sorts of things".
Jules Desmond is an experimental musician who has played in bands including Letterbox Lambs, 1/3 Octave Band, Bachelor of Architecture and Black Boned Angel.

Amy Jean Barnett is a composer and artist working with sound, performance, installation and acoustic ecology in her practice.
Barnett's live performances weave intricate narratives through sound, drawing on electroacoustic techniques, minimalism, and field recordings. Working with recorded fragments, improvisation, and a tactile engagement with materials, she creates auditory environments of shifting textures that invite deep listening and reveal the subtle complexities of sound unfolding over time.
Barnett is currently pursuing a Master of Musical Arts at the New Zealand School of Music under the supervision of Michael Norris.

description:
Deafheaven & Nothing | Wellington | San Fran, Deafheaven & Nothing | Wellington | San Fran
American black-metal trailblazers Deafheaven announce their return to New Zealand this July, presented by Banished Music. The band will perform two exclusive headline shows in Auckland and Wellington, joined by special guests Nothing.
‍
Formed in the San Francisco Bay Area in 2010, Deafheaven have spent the past decade and a half pushing at the emotional and sonic boundaries of modern metal. From their debut Roads to Judah, to the genre-defining breakthrough Sunbather, and subsequent records like New Bermuda, Ordinary Corrupt Human Love, and Infinite Granite, Deafheaven have continually redefined the limits of heavy music while confronting themes of alienation, addiction, family history, and self-perseverance.
‍
The tour follows the release of their 2025 album Lonely People With Power. Their sixth album and first for Roadrunner Records arrives as both a culmination and a reckoning , an album that embraces the band’s full identity after years of evolution. Produced by Justin Meldal-Johnsen (Beck collaborator and producer of Infinite Granite), the record captures Deafheaven’s innate ability to merge melody with brutality, and pain with poetry. Through reflections on masculinity, inherited trauma, family, and self-perception, the album grapples with the idea that while we can’t fully escape our past or our nature, we can choose how we move forward. Ultimately, Lonely People With Power stands as one of Deafheaven’s most expansive and human statements.
‍
The album has drawn praise from Pitchfork, Rolling Stone, The Line Of Best Fit, Kerrang and more, and features collaborations with Interpol’s Paul Banks and Boy Harsher’s Jae Matthews.
‍
Revered for their transcendental live shows, Deafheaven have toured the world over, performing at festivals such as Coachella and Primavera Sound, and sharing stages with artists ranging from Slipknot and Knocked Loose to Chelsea Wolfe and Mono. They’ve received a Grammy Award nomination for Best Metal Performance and continue to command a reputation as one of the most compelling live acts in heavy music.
‍
Joining them are American shoegaze outfit Nothing, whose latest release A Short History of Decay has been described by Pitchfork as “fresh and exciting.” Their fifth album and first for Run For Cover Records further expands the band’s sonic scope, delivering the most refined and immersive iteration of Nothing to date.
‍
Deafheaven return to New Zealand at their most expansive and unrelenting. Don’t miss the chance to witness one of heavy music’s most boundary-pushing bands at full force.

Tom Cunliffe writes folk songs like short films; vivid, offbeat, and full of heart. Based in Tamaki Makaurau, Auckland, he crafts lyrical worlds, with a guitar tuned sideways and a voice that balances gravity with joy.

Cunliffe has supported a number of internationally renowned artists including M. Ward, Grace Cummings, and Reb Fountain, bringing his mix of warmth, wit, and slow-burning intensity to stages near and far.

Ali Whitton is an Aotearoa-born, Yorkshire-raised and now Wellington based singer-songwriter who is stepping into his own as an artist. Ali is an artist who refuses to let go, blending raw storytelling with a sound shaped by decades of experience and dedication to his craft.

Performing for years under the name Lost Bird, Ali built a reputation for writing heartfelt, melancholic folk-pop, playing everywhere from Wellington bars to stadium stages — including opening for Ed Sheeran in Auckland in 2018.

This immersive masterclass is designed for curious explorers, hobby photographers and anyone who has ever looked up and wished they could capture what they saw.

Your instructor is an experienced astro-educator, and you’ll be taken step by step through the art and science of night-sky photography with DSLR or mirrorless cameras. You’ll learn how to focus at infinity, choose the best camera settings, build compositions under the Milky Way, and work with RAW files, noise control and exposure strategy. You’ll photograph live star fields and leave with images you can genuinely be proud of.

No astronomy expertise or prior astrophotography experience is required — just your curiosity. Bring a camera and tripod if you have them, but if not, you can still attend, learn from telescope-linked imaging feeds, and gain the skills and confidence to shoot the cosmos on your own.

Held at Star Safari, right in the Wairarapa dark-sky heartlands, this experience takes place under the same southern skies recognised by Lonely Planet as one of the world’s top stargazing destinations. If you’ve ever wanted to try astrophotography, this is the moment, and this is the place.

What you’ll gain:
- Confidence to shoot the night sky
- Proven camera settings and workflow
- Real photos of the Milky Way and southern star fields
- Knowledge you can use anywhere the southern sky is visible
- A rare, premium learning experience under a world-class sky

Perfect for couples, travellers, creatives, astronomy lovers, and anyone who wants a deeper connection to the night.

Spaces are limited to keep the experience personal.

We'll look at the tools available on Ancestry.com and other DNA websites to help you use DNA for your family's history.

Got your test results back and still wondering what a centiMorgan or a shared match is? Find out what the size of your match means and the tools available to help you work out possible family relationships.

We'll start by looking at Clustering and how the Grouping tool on Ancestry.com can help with this. We'll also look at the ThruLines and Common Ancestors tools to see how they can provide suggestions for knocking down brick walls in your research.

Also covered during this course are other websites you can upload your results to, how to manage other family member's DNA test results and other tools available when you get a bit more advanced - and just in case you need help in the future, we'll look at some of the places you could get this from.

Please note: This course will only cover DNA tests taken through Ancestry.com

Bring a USB stick and your Ancestry.com login details.

By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:
- Understand the information provided by Ancestry.com about your DNA matches
- Use the Grouping, ThruLines and Common Ancestors tools on Ancestry.com
- Use the Shared CentiMorgan tool on DNAPainter.com
- Understand where to find other tools
- Understand the options for using other DNA websites
- Understand where to get further help

Prerequisites
For those who have already done a DNA test through Ancestry.com
You will need good computing and internet skills.

description:
EC-MENz Summit 2026, EC-MENz vision is for men fully participating at all levels of Early Childhood Education to represent the diversity of our society in Aotearoa.
The EC-MENz Summit 2026 is kindly being hosted and supported by Childspace.

Tāne, wāhine, and irawhiti are warmly invited to participate in a special day of high quality, affordable professional learning. This celebration of gender diversity in ECE will be held in a safe and supportive environment and is a fantastic opportunity to meet others in the profession, share your own story, and be inspired.
Gender Steretoypes in ECE - Mike Collin and Max Christie
What can gender stereotypes teach us about teaching and learning?
Early childhood education relies on diversity within teaching teams. Yet, gender stereotypes often shape how we see ourselves and each other as kaiako. This interactive session invites educators to explore the hidden assumptions that influence teaching roles and team dynamics. In this session, Max and Mike will unpack how stereotypes impact collaboration and how every kaiako adds unique value to teaching teams. Participants will leave with practical strategies to challenge bias, strengthen team culture, and celebrate the richness of varied approaches in ECE settings.
Autism NZ - Thecla Moffat
Men can change the dynamics of play in ECE benefiting autistic tamariki
Male kaiako often bring more energy in the ECE setting with an emphasis on more physical activity, outdoor play, "rough and tumble" play, and positive risk-taking, which appeals to both boys and girls and provides a different dimension to play than may be beneficial to most autistic tamariki. We now know that through fun and engaging interactions kaiako help enhance the autistic tamariki pivotal capacities for later learning. In this talk kaiako will get to know how men in ECE with their positive energy can make a difference through play for autistic tamariki in their centres. The kaiako will be given a few strategies of how to do that and some ideas to encourage tuakana-teina (peer play) between autistic tamariki and their non-autistic peers will be shared.

Guided by our experienced and supportive tutors, you’ll be introduced to the fundamental skills of jewellery-making while creating a small collection of rings to take home and treasure.

During this 3-hour class, you’ll learn how to measure your finger, cut metal to size, and add textures and patterns using hammers and punches. From there, you’ll be shown how to solder your rings together with a jeweller’s torch before finishing them with filing, sanding and polishing techniques. Along the way, our tutors will share tips and tricks, patiently guiding you so you feel confident every step of the way.

By the end of the session, you’ll have crafted two sterling silver rings and two copper or brass rings, and if time allows, you can make even more!

Each ring you make is completely your own, whether you keep them sleek and simple or experiment with texture and pattern. You’ll leave not only with a stylish, wearable ring stack, but also with the joy of having made something truly unique with your own hands.

This class is perfect for beginners, groups of friends, or visitors wanting a memorable creative experience. Many students find jewellery making a wonderfully mindful activity - slowing down, working with their hands and enjoying the calming rhythm of making.

Your class fee includes copper and brass for practice, sterling silver for two rings, plus all consumables such as solder, sandpaper and polishing materials. Extra silver and other metals are available for purchase in the studio if you’d like to expand your collection.

Children aged 12 and up are welcome, though anyone under 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver.

Monday Eve 8 Week Block - Mixed Levels, Our popular weeknight block classes are the best way for keen makers to get into jewellery making in a lively, warm and friendly environment. This class will be held at our new waterfront location, Market Lane!

This class is a mixed-level class, allowing beginners to work alongside advanced students. It is the best way for beginners to get into jewellery-making in a lively, warm and friendly environment.

Beginners start with basic ring-making and stone-setting in copper or brass. Students will learn measuring, texturing, shaping, cutting and soldering. Then we move on to making a practice-ring set with a Cabochon stone (cabochon means it has a flat bottom and a smooth domed top) in a Bezel Setting. As you work through your practice ring and setting, you can move on to working in silver and produce another ring with a cabochon stone that you really love.

Level 2 students learn to solder more competently on their own using chainmaking as a way to develop their fine soldering skills. They may create a simple stone setting or ring alongside this challenge project so they have something to hone their skills that they are familiar with, as well as taking on a new skill.

Level 3 and above students are encouraged to work on their design skills and try new and challenging techniques. They should prepare to have one or two simple projects they can work on self-directed in class, alongside a challenge project.

This class fee does NOT include materials for any student.

Beginners should expect to spend at least $60 on materials for their ring making project.
All metals and stones as well as quality findings and chains are available for purchase each week in the studio. Students are encouraged to keep their silver scrap and find ways to use it thriftily in future projects!

It’s a wonderful chance to engage with new ideas.
They will be at our club on Wednesday 26 November at 5.30pm (for a 6pm presentation). It is part of a project on “Science, Culture and Economy – Links between Croatian Communities in the World and the Homeland”.
The presentations are on:
- Brief history of Croatian standard language – Prof. Luka Budak (former Head of Croatian Studies, Macquarie University);
- World-renowned Croatian scientists and inventors – Dr. Marijana Borić, Scientific Advisor (Croatian Academy of Sciences and Arts – CASA);
- The Croatian economy from 1992 to the present day – Prof. Tomislava Majić, Senior Lecturer (University North); and
- Croatian language recognition in Australia in 1970s – Prof. Ana Bruning (former lecturer at Croatian Studies, Macquarie University and long-time Croatian language teacher at the Croatian Schools in Sydney.
The presenters acknowledge the support of Croatian Studies Foundation of Australia, Central State Office for Croats Outside of the Republic of Croatia, Foundation of Croatian Academy of Sciences and Arts.
Current timings for the event are:
5:30pm - gather for tea/coffee/drinks
6:00pm - Presentations
This will be followed by a question and discussion time, with a light supper and drinks.
All welcome! You don't need to be a member of the Club to attend!

description:
Richard Dawkins — 50 Years of The Selfish Gene, Richard Dawkins is a world-renowned evolutionary biologist. When published in 1976, his book, ‘The Selfish Gene’, reframed our understanding of life, behaviour, and human nature. Now, 50 years later, he is coming to Wellington to reflect on the book’s revolutionary legacy. He explores what fifty years of science has confirmed or challenged and explains why its core questions are more urgent today than ever before. 
‘The Selfish Gene’ has remained a cornerstone of modern science. It introduced the gene-centred view of evolution and coined the now-ubiquitous concept of the ‘meme’. The ideas in it ignited global debate and five decades of subsequent research. Richard Dawkins is one of the most consequential scientific communicators of our time, so don’t miss the rare opportunity to hear him speak in person.

description:
International Women's Day Lunch, We are very excited to bring to you the 2026 International Women's Lunch along with our supporting sponsor Wakefields Lawyers.
It's that time of year to get some friends, work mates together and come along, enjoy and celebrate International Women's Day 2026.
We are excited to be welcoming Suzanne Paul as our Guest Speaker for 2026.
Inspirational speaker Suzanne Paul arrived in New Zealand from the working-class streets of Wolverhampton in 1991 with just $18 in her pocket and a fierce determination to succeed.
Despite the challenges of a learning disability that brought anxiety and low self-esteem, Suzanne channelled her boundless optimism and natural gift for sales into building one of the country’s most successful direct marketing empires. Her iconic products, such as Natural Glow and the Suzanne Clip, became household names, and within five years, she had transformed herself into a multimillionaire and one of New Zealand’s most beloved public figures, complete with her own TV shows. In 2007, she further captured the nation’s heart by winning Dancing with the Stars.
Life took a dramatic turn at 50 when Suzanne lost everything and was declared bankrupt. Though tempted to give up, she instead drew on the same resilience and skills that had built her earlier success. Starting over from nothing, she rebuilt her life step by step, launching new ventures and embracing fresh challenges.
Among her many accomplishments since then, Suzanne developed a clothing line for petite women, opened a boutique in Remuera, and spearheaded the success of Thin Lizzy Makeup in both New Zealand and Australia. She also became a bestselling author with But Wait, There’s More, a book that shares her journey and practical wisdom on making dreams come true. A second edition is currently in the works, focusing on resilience and turning intention into action.
Now living her dream life once again, Suzanne Paul continues to prove that even in the face of adversity, reinvention is always possible—and that success is never out of reach.
Join us for a delicious lunch by Party Perfect, network and have a great time!

description:
You Spot It You Got It: Unpacking cultural conditioning and turning the mirror inwards, Talanoa Tai Learning is a new collection of learning experiences. They're designed to help you build your cultural responsiveness and improve your ability to engage meaningfully with Pacific communities. Talanoa is a Pacific style of deep dialogue, with a focus on how we connect to each other and strengthen relationships, while still being able to share honest and effective insights. If you want to strengthen your capability in this space, to create transformational change, and to enhance your relationships with people from different communities - this workshop is your chance to grow.
What will I gain from You Spot It, You Got It?
In You Spot It, You Got It, you will deepen self-awareness by being encouraged to recognise some of your own conditioning and impacts of this in your daily life/practices. When we are not conscious of the things that might not sit right within us then we unknowingly or knowingly project them onto others. What we reject, we project. By examining patterns and recognising our conditioning, then we can truly understand how we can live in more conscious ways. This Talanoa Tai learning experience offers space for talanoa, tools and exercises to facilitate introspection and personal growth by turning the mirror inwards.
This is a 3.5 hour in-person learning experience. The day will start with a mihi whakatau to welcome you into the space.
Who is this workshop for?
These learning experiences are for both Paciﬁc professionals and those from other communities. You don’t need to have prior knowledge or experience in this area - we’ll meet you where you are and provide a welcoming, supportive environment for you to learn.
Cultural responsiveness is for everyone. Whether you’re in social work, education, government, community sectors or beyond, these learning experiences have been designed to help everyone build their skills. If you think this professional development might be right for you, it is!
Cost
When work is busy and budgets are tight, cultural responsiveness can often take a backseat. But this is an aﬀordable investment that will help you address the challenges that so many of us share, like how to build engagement and trust, and avoid relationship missteps. It’s not a buzzword; it’s a vital skill if you want to better meet the needs of the people you serve. Price: $170 (inc GST) per person, including morning tea.
Facilitator
Our team’s extensive research and experience feed into these sessions, with a focus on interactive activities and practical, real-life examples. Our team has decades of experience across a range of ﬁelds, in particular social development, education, and research. We have worked with organisations and businesses across the Paciﬁc, and our engagement with diﬀerent Paciﬁc languages, cultures, and communities means we oﬀer robust, informed perspectives. Fa’aeafale’upolu (Polu) Samuelu is the facilitator of this Talanoa Tai Learning experience.

Chess – Learn to Play, Chess is an ancient game of strategy and analysis that hones concentration and focus, as you master the skills allowing you to win at this competitive recreation.
Join tutor, Ryan Hill to learn how to play this game from the beginning.
You will quickly go from understanding the basics to being able to engage in playing confidently and discover where to go for further training or to carry on playing – both in person and online.
Over 600 million people play this game that has remained popular throughout the ages – why don’t you become one of them!
Bring pen and paper to take notes.
By the end of this course you will be able to:
*Be able to use all of the chess pieces to play the game
*Be able to recount and use some of the most common openings and traps
*Recognise where to go for further training or to play
*Develop increasing levels of confidence in your ability to play and possibly win

description:
Contract Law Fundamentals for Non Lawyers Masterclass Wellington, Contract Law Fundamentals for Non Lawyers Masterclass Wellington
Register Today by contacting Crown Leadership International Group: Website: www.crownleadership.com.au Phone: +64 9 889 7217

About this Event

Contract Law Fundamentals for Non Lawyers Masterclass is an intensely practical guide through the essentials of contract law, exploring such details as when a contract will be required, when you have a contract (and don’t necessarily know it), what types of contract exist and the effect of legislation on your contractual arrangements.
This masterclass also scrutinises what happens when things go wrong, including how you can get out of a contract, options for assessing damages and remedies for breach and looking at the contractual implications of working in an e-commerce environment. You will grasp the crucial ingredients required for a good contract, and gain tips to better understand and manage your contracts.

description:
Your Life’s Purpose – Discover Your Emotional Needs and Core Values, Your Life’s Purpose – Discover Your Emotional Needs and Core Values
(NZ Citizens and residents pay $49 with ID, all others pay $120).
Put in the hard work on this one day Saturday workshop and experience the benefits of self-knowledge. Let the emotional knowledge you gain inform not only how you live your life but also how you feel about living it. You’ll be asking the big questions about not only how you live your life, but also why. Discover the tools and scientifically based information to inform the exploration of your life’s purpose.
Consider your emotional needs and how they relate to personal meaning. You’ll unwrap the concepts of emotional nutrition and be shown how to be guided by your values and start to think of them as a compass directing the journey of your life. To do this you’ll identify your values hierarchy and learn about how this framework can inform how you live your life. Once you can apply a spirit of consistency to your self-identified larger purpose, as well as your needs, then your life’s purpose, emotional needs and core values, will align. It’s quite a transformational day!
Bring pen and paper.  Tea and coffee provided, please bring your lunch/snacks.
NOTE: This course is subsidised with funding from the Tertiary Education Commission (TEC) and you must provide photo ID when you attend your first session, if applicable.
By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:
Develop a Life Purpose Statement
Perform an Emotional Needs Self-Assessment
Elicit Your Core Values
Align your goals with your life purpose, emotional needs and core values

description:
2026 Wellington POCUS Fundamentals Course / EGLS Course, POCUS Fundamentals + EGLS
2 Days of Comprehensive POCUS education for Acute Care Clinicians
Take part in a flexible learning experience designed for real-world acute care:
Day 1: POCUS Fundamentals
Master the essentials – focus on AAA & eFAST.
Day 2: EGLS (Echo Guided Life Support)
Confidently assess and manage the shocked patient using focused cardiac and lung ultrasound.
Attend either day independently, or combine both for a complete acute care ultrasound experience.

Day 1 – POCUS Fundamentals
Focus on essential diagnostic ultrasound skills with Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm (AAA) & eFAST (extended Focused Assessment with Sonography in Trauma) modules. This is ideal for clinicians seeking to build confidence and competence in core applications that can be immediately applied in clinical practice.
https://www.emugs.org/pocusfundamentals
Day 2 – EGLS (Echo-Guided Life Support)
Take your resuscitation skills to the next level with EGLS. Learn a structured, protocolised approach to using cardiac and lung ultrasound in the assessment and management of shock and respiratory failure. This course is designed to empower acute care clinicians with the practical skills to make rapid, life-saving decisions.
https://www.emugs.org/egls
Combo of Fundamentals + EGLS - Whether you're new to ultrasound or looking to enhance your skills, this comprehensive two-day course  is ideal for acute care clinicians aiming to integrate POCUS into daily practice.
You'll cover the core emergency medicine ultrasound modules: FELS, eFAST, AAA, and lung. The course aligns with ACEM and ASUM credentialing requirements for core ultrasound modalities.
By the end, you'll be proficient in four essential techniques: focused echo in life support (FELS), extended FAST, aortic scanning, and lung/thoracic ultrasound.
The program includes online pre-course work, brief lectures, image review, hands-on scanning, and networking opportunities—all within a supportive learning environment.
Suitable for all experience levels:
ACEM trainees beginning their ultrasound journey
Acute care doctors looking to upskill
Clinicians in critical care, rural, and urgent care settings
Beginners will build a solid foundation; experienced users can refine skills with expert feedback

description:
Kia Mau, Kia Mau is an arts festival that showcases innovative Indigenous performances. Held every two years, the festival lights up Wellington's winter. See contemporary performances by leading Tāngata Whenua , Tāngata Moana, and global Indigenous artists. The two-week festival includes dance, theatre, music, and visual art. Audiences can expect to be challenged and thrilled by new work from Aotearoa and beyond.
Kia Mau was first held in 2015, founded by two leading Aotearoa creatives. Hone Kouka (Ngāti Porou, Ngāti Kahungunu, Ngāti Raukawa, Kai Tahu) is the Artistic Director and Chief Executive. Mīria George (Ngāti Kearoa, Ngāti Tuara, Ngāti Awa, Ngāti Kūki ‘Āirani) is the Executive Director.
Hone and Mīria describe themselves as innovators. They push boundaries, redefine forms, and forge new paths. They say the festival is not just a platform for presentations, it’s a hub for kōrero and whanaungatanga . The festival has a strong influence on many artists and plays an important role in shaping New Zealand’s contemporary arts scene. “Kia Mau has continued to thrive because of the imagination and commitment of our artists. And of us to them,” says Mīria.

Slow Grind Fever [AUS] - Wellington Jazz Festival, Express from Melbourne, Australia and crossing international waters for the first time this October, Meow is excited to welcome the slowest, spookiest, smokiest and swingin-est club night Wellington has ever seen: 'Slow Grind Fever'.
For this one-night-only episode of SGF Wellington, founder Richie1250 (106.7 PBS FM) will be joined by fellow Melbourne radio alumnus Dr. Popalotacorn (RRR, 98.1FM Raglan) and Wellington's own belle of the airwaves Miss Juliet (RadioActive.FM Americana)
Slow Grind Fever was born in 2012 when Richie1250 hired a Russian Cultural Centre ballroom and threw a slow dance party for his 30th birthday, and it's been running as a regular monthly club night ever since. Richie and his friends play the slowest, sleaziest, spookiest, sweetest, swinginest old records they can find, and people dance real slow in a haze of smoke and dim red light. It's a good time.
In the last few years Richie has taken Slow Grind Fever on the road, with regular dances in Sydney, Hobart, Darwin and Alice Springs. They post up a monthly Slow Grind Fever mix in the week before the party every month, and have collaborated with Stag-O Lee Records in Germany on a series of Slow Grind Fever LPs and CDs.
Enjoy the music and if you feel so inclined, get down to Slow Grind Fever - Wellington at Meow on Friday 17th October.
Listening to the MP3 mixes is nice, but when you’re in the room all
wrapped up in smoke with the music sizzling right off the old records, through the speakers and into your brain, well, there's nothing quite like it…

National Celebration - 40 Years of Homosexual Law Reform, National Celebration - 40 Years of Homosexual Law Reform
40 Years of Homosexual Law Reform – Community Celebration at Parliament

Join us in the historic Banquet Hall at Parliament as we come together to celebrate 40 years since the passing of the Homosexual Law Reform Act — a landmark moment that helped transform Aotearoa New Zealand into a more inclusive and just society.

This special evening will honour the courage, determination, and advocacy of those who fought for equality, while celebrating the vibrant and diverse rainbow communities who continue that legacy today.

The programme will feature speeches from past and present activists, sharing reflections on the movement, the challenges faced, and the progress achieved over four decades. Guests will also enjoy performances from talented members of the community, bringing music, storytelling, and creative expression to the celebration.

More than a commemoration, this event is also an opportunity to connect across generations of the rainbow community and allies. Join activists, community leaders, supporters, and friends for an evening of reflection, celebration, and whakawhanaungatanga in one of the country’s most significant civic spaces.

Together, we honour the past, celebrate the present, and look toward a future where equality and inclusion continue to grow.

About this Event



Ultimate Tribute Fest 2: A Memorial for Metal Legends

Rail Records, Wildkiwi Distillery, Women's Refuge, and Riockstock present a monumental night of heavy metal in honor of two of the genre's most important and beloved figures: the legendary guitarist "Dimebag" Darrell Abbott of Pantera, and the recently departed Godfather of Metal, Ozzy Osbourne.
Join us on Saturday, December 6th, 2025, at Wildkiwi in Upper Hutt for a memorial show that will shake the foundations. This date holds a special importance to us metal heads, falling just three days after what would have been Ozzy's 77th birthday (December 3rd) and just two days before the anniversary of Dimebag's tragic passing (December 8th, 2004), giving us all a chance to raise a glass and celebrate both legends in the loudest way possible.
This is a night to pay tribute to the artists who defined a generation of heavy music. From Dimebag's revolutionary groove and unmistakable harmonic squeals to Ozzy's haunting vocals and iconic stage presence, their impact is eternal. We invite the metal community to come together for an unforgettable evening of remembrance, unity, and blistering riffs.

Coven: Wet - Pride Party, Follow the siren song to Ivy Bar this Pride Festival and get pool ready for a night that will leave you dripping. This is a pride dance party for sapphic, trans, nonbinary, and gender-diverse people, so let's get wet with pride.
You don’t want to miss the tantalising surprises we have planned… Follow us on Instagram for more teasers.

Coven is pay as you wish or koha on the door.
More info about Coven:
Coven Kaupapa
For queer women and gender minorities, spaces like this are rare, vital, and sometimes, life-changing. In a world that constantly centers cishet norms, Coven offers a space where we are the default – where you can fully show up as yourself, be seen, celebrated and surrounded by YOUR community.
Coming Solo? You’re Not Alone.
Don’t be nervous if you’re planning to come on your own – Coven is built for connection. Whether it’s your first queer event or your hundredth, you’ll be surrounded by a community that gets it. From the moment you arrive, there’ll be friendly faces, welcoming vibes, and plenty of chances to mingle, and connect. Coven is about belonging – and there’s a place here for you.
For many in our Coven, this is one of the only opportunities we feel comfortable enough to experience nightlife free from the male gaze, tokenism, fear, or the need to shrink ourselves to fit in. It’s a space where sapphic, trans, nonbinary, and gender-diverse people aren’t just welcomed – we are centered. It’s for those who are often pushed to the margins, who rarely feel represented in “inclusive” spaces that still cater to the mainstream.
This night exists because we need it – and because we create it, together.

description:
24-hour Squash Marathon for Wayne, 24 Hours on Court for Wayne.
This time I’m picking up my squash racket for a challenge like no other: 24 hours of nonstop squash. Why? Because someone I care for has been facing a far tougher battle.
My father-in-law was recently diagnosed with Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL). For years he lived undiagnosed, pushing through symptoms without answers. Now that we finally know what he’s fighting, I want to turn my energy into something that can help him—and others—on their journeys.
According to CLL Advocates NZ, only 10-15 people out of 250 on average per year benefit from the budget allocation. And many are not even able to receive the same treatment options here in NZ.
Squash has always been a sport of endurance, resilience, and determination. Playing for 24 hours is my way of honoring his fight, raising awareness, and bringing people together to support the cause.
You can help by:
Donating: Any amount you would like to.
Predicting: Predicting how many points and games will be played in 24 hours.
Joining me on court: Book a slot to play a game, cheer from the sidelines, or come be part of the atmosphere.
Buy raffle tickets, or sponsor a prize towards the raffle.
We would like to give a shout out to our current sponsors;
Hair Phoria,
Aimee Photography,
X-Potential,
Mitchells,
Meaters,
CBD Eatery,
Forrest Wines and
Fat Tony's
No matter how small, your contribution will make a difference. Together we can transform his story of late diagnosis into one of community, awareness, and action.
I’ll be pushing myself through the night, but I won’t be alone—your support will keep me going with every serve, rally, and game. Let’s make this 24 hours count.

description:
10th Grade Tournament, 10th Grade Tournament
10th Grade Tournament

Timona Park, Feilding | Hosted by Feilding United AFC Juniors

Feilding United AFC invites all 10th Grade teams registered to play in Central Football Manawatū to attend the 2026 10th Grade Festival in Feilding.

There is a 10th Grade Cup to be won, with runner-up medals awarded for second place. A minimum of eight teams is required for both awards to be presented.

No academy teams or tournament specific teams to enter.

WHEN & WHERE

The festival will be held on: Sunday 21 June 2026
(Postponement date: Sunday 28 June 2026)

📍 Timona Park, Feilding – Home of Feilding United AFC Juniors

· 8:30am – Coaches Meeting at the Feilding AFC Gazebo

· 9:00am – First games kick off

REGISTRATIONS

Registrations must be completed via Tournify using the link below:

https://tournifyapp.com/live/feildingafc10thgradetournament

Registration fee: $110 per team

The first 16 teams registered by 8th June 2026 will secure a place in the tournament.

RULES

Tournament rules will follow the current Central Football Regulations for Youth Leagues, which can be viewed here:

https://www.sporty.co.nz/asset/downloadasset?id=7eabcc5d-0023-4a42-9383-cb93c07e4814

DRAW & FORMAT

· Teams will play a minimum of four games.

· Games will consist of:

o 2 x 10-minute halves

o 2 -minute halftime

Points System

· Win = 3 points

· Draw = 1 point

The team with the most points will win their group.

If teams are tied on points, placings will be determined by:

1. Goal difference

2. Most goals scored

3. Toss of a coin

If a semi-final or final ends in a draw, the match will go directly to a penalty shootout. No extra time will be played.

REFEREES

Referees will be provided for most games. However, if a referee is unavailable, teams may be asked to provide a suitable person to control one half of the game.

The referee’s decision is final.

POSTPONEMENTS / CANCELLATIONS

The tournament will proceed regardless of weather conditions unless:

· Manawatū District Council closes the grounds, or

· A Health & Safety risk is identified by the Feilding United AFC Junior Football Committee.

Please remember that everyone involved in organising and refereeing this tournament are volunteers. Without them, this event could not take place.

Enjoy the day and the opportunity to watch the kids play the beautiful game!

description:

Please note that this is a rally, and not a race. So, you need to follow provided instructions, and answer questions along the way correctly to win a prize. There is no prize for being the fastest. This rally has been organized for the Kapiti chapter of the MX-5 Club of NZ, but any other MX-5 drivers are welcome. Details below:

We will be meeting at the same place as last time - the Park 'n' Ride carpark at Manor Park, Lower Hutt, at 9am. Don't worry - we'll be doing completely different roads this time!

There is no breakfast at the start, but if people are interested, we could informally meet at Town & Country in Stokes Valley for breakfast beforehand,then all drive to the Park 'n' Ride together in convoy.

You will need to bring a pen or pencil, and something to press on, such as a clipboard, or a hardcover book. You will also need something you can take evidence photos with - a cellphone or digital camera will be fine.

I also highly, highly recommend that you bring a co-driver, as it will make things infinitely easier for you. Call Russell on 021 0269 3224 if you have trouble finding a co-driver, as I can assist with that!

Like last time, there will be prizes for 1st, 2nd & 3rd, but the prizes are based on who gets the most answers correct, and NOT on who is fastest to complete the course.

Lunch will be at the end point, so bring some $$$ with you.

Snacks will again be provided along the way. This event is free for members of The Kapiti Chapter of the MX-5 Club of NZ, or $2 per car for non-members of that club. This will cover the cost of the provided snacks, plus the photocopying. Thanks.

Further instructions on the day, but if you attended the last rally I organised, then you'll know what to expect. You'll need about 1/2 a tank of gas.

Please RSVP to Russell by texting 021 0269 3224 by Friday 13 Feb, so I can ensure that there are enough printed instructions for everyone.

Wairarapa Walking Festival 2025: Gladstone Wine and Olive Walk, Back by popular demand, the much-loved Gladstone Wine & Olive Walk is a relaxed, sensory journey through one of Wairarapa’s most celebrated wine-growing areas. Stroll the river terraces above the Ruamāhanga, where award-winning vineyards and olive groves flourish, and enjoy tastings of wines, olive oils, and seasonal nibbles along the way.

Guided through vines and groves, you’ll gain insights into why Gladstone wines are consistently praised for their complexity and elegance, shaped by the region’s unique soils and growing conditions. Highlights include a stop at the stunning Urlar Vineyard cellar door, recently awarded Gold at the 2025 Master Builders Commercial Project Awards, and stories of Gladstone’s history shared en route. This walk is led by local Gladstone legend John Booth, in partnership with the Go Carterton business group.

This walk is via bus only, due to parking restrictions and road safety. The bus will leave the Wairarapa Events Centre at 2pm and return at 5pm. Plan ahead - Please ensure you organise safe transport home from the Wairarapa Events Centre.

Join us at 8:30am on Sunday 21 September for the next edition of the Honest 10 taking in Wellington's beautiful waterfront. The Honest 10 is the perfect chance to test your 5km or 10km fitness and maybe have a go at walking or running PB.
EVERYONE IS WELCOME NO MATTER WHAT YOUR LEVEL OF FITNESS. The is an optional 8:15am early start for those who think they might need more time (eg over 70 mins for 10k)

Steffanie Holmes' Wellington Book Launch: A Grave Mistake, Steffanie Holmes' Book Launch of 'A Grave Mistake'.
The second book in The Nevermore Murder Club & Smutty Book Coven series.

Interconnected standalone series about the members of a supernatural book club finding their happily-ever-afters in a small town infested with vampires. Set in the same world as the Nevermore Bookshop, but eight years after.
Steffanie Holmes is a USA TODAY bestselling author of paranormal romance, urban fantasy, and supernatural mysteries. Her books feature clever, witty heroines, dark and gothy settings, cunning witches, and a dash of sadistic humour.
A Grave Mistake is the second book in The Nevermore Murder Club & Smutty Book Coven series, following Fangs for Nothing. This cosy paranormal romance blends enemy vampires who were once lovers, a meddling book club, a murder mystery, and more tea than should be legal, all with darkly witty, vampy charm.
Arabella Lestrange was once the most notorious dancer in Paris’ underground vampire cabaret, until she fell for a human, Gideon Blake, and he ruined her afterlife. She fled certain he wouldn’t survive long… only to encounter him 150 years later, newly undead and just as infuriatingly charming. It’s a story of revenge, romance, immortality, and meddling friends - all with a darkly witty twist.
This is a second-chance romance with the first romance happening in 18th-century Belle Epoque Paris, where the heroine is a pole dancer at a vampire cabaret (Le Petite Mort). Which means the launch needs a stage worthy of vampires and pole dancers alike...

description:
The Foragers – Opening, Twentysix Gallery is pleased to present ‘The Foragers’, a solo exhibition featuring new works by Emma Hercus.
Growing up we used to hunt and gather. Rabbits, goats, eels, trout, deer - blackberries, walnuts, macadamias, plums and roadside apples. Dad would make my brother and I rabbit stew and blackberry milkshakes, while our neighbour Mike would smoke the eels till they were buttery and tasted of the earth. The land gives with an outstretched hand and Emma Hercus composes from within it. Both bush and coastlines, fields and roadside corners unfold in ‘The Foragers’.
Painting in oil and true to form, Hercus’ portraits are wide-eyed and poignant. Rosy cheeks with head scarfs and fur vests, a striped shirt paired with a tight lipped smirk. Once, when young and curious, we foraged for blue mushrooms - found on the tree line of native bush - we made a bitter tasting tea. It was a strange and vivid afternoon. I painted a lot. This series dipping into rich colour - her skies are energetic, the ocean layered and deep. Foliage is defined and vivacious, sharp and encompassing for all its inhabitants inside. For Hercus, the landscape and its fauna are at her core.
Before the walnuts were about to fall, my mother would thump the giant trees with a chain - beat them into shape to bear more fruit. It is a life sustained by the earth, a bloodline of foragers and a childhood of lessons in how to continue to do so. These days we live by the sea, white baiting season bringing the people of the coast together in the same spot every year. Sustenance from the hunt - sustenance from the community that gathers around the table to share foraged, grown, caught and collected kai. The gratification in sharing both a meal and a memory.
The exhibition runs from 27 February – 21 March 2026, with an opening celebration on Thursday, 26 February at 6pm.

Be prepared for textured sound and thought gymnastics with Riki on the drums and Bennett on the mic, closing out the series with one epic jam from these two legends.

5:30pm Doors open, bar open

6:45pm Artist Q&A
7pm Closing Karakia and time to explore He Kura Toi Tangata exhibition

Te Waka Huia Wellington Museum

Thursday 18 September | 6pm–8pm

Tickets: $25–$35


About Riki Gooch

Dr Riki Neihana Gooch lives in Te Whanganui-a-Tara, Aotearoa. His work spans multiple disciplines, including composition, performance, sound art, production, and academic research. He has led and conducted large-scale ensemble projects, performed in a wide range of collaborative settings, and created work for both recorded and live contexts. His ongoing projects include solo and group performances, conduction ensembles, DJ sets, and sound-based installations. He is also involved in cultural leadership and mentorship roles, holding wānanga and contributing to intergenerational knowledge exchange within the arts.


About Bennett Pomana

Bennett Pomana (Te Aitanga-a-Māhaki, Ngāi Tāmanuhiri) is a musician raised in Upper Hutt, with roots in Tūranganui-a-Kiwa. A longtime contributor to Aotearoa’s hip hop legacy, he has been part of pioneering groups including Upper Hutt Posse and Dam Native. His work is deeply influenced by his Māori identity, drawing inspiration from whakapapa, lived experience, and the ongoing pursuit of justice and expression through sound.


This event has been developed by Te Waka Huia Wellington Museum and is presented in collaboration with our programme partner Kāhui Legal.

description:
Here Comes The Fencing Act 1979!, 
Wellington chamber pop orchestra the Sven Olsens return to the Fringe with another sonic slice of life in Aotearoa/New Zealand. The 18-strong collective has spent the past 15 years recording over 100 songs about what makes people in this country tick. They are still none the wiser but now twice the poorer.
This band presents material others sensibly avoid. They've created an 'ear-worm' farm using topics as varied as: the Fencing Act 1979, ever-elusive Hasting's tagger Kron, Huka Falls' boogie boarding dare devil Dr. Bubbles, the perils of kung fu dancing on top of chicken restaurants and the influence of 19th century painting on the hangovers of local librarians.
The Svens will sing 70 mins worth of material from their endless 'magnum 'opeless'. This show will be a celebration of national quirks, perks and potholes, baffling and fascinating in equal measure, gloriously short and to the point. There'll be strings, choir and a band. There'll be a multimedia extravaganza. There'll be merch. And there'll be you. This Svens' motto is 'one last shot at obscurity'. This is your chance to prove them wrong.

The animals of Manor Farm have had enough. They rise up, and build a new world on the promise that all animals are equal. But it won't last.

Toi Whakaari: NZ Drama School presents Animal Farm by Van Badham, as part of our 2026 Double Bill season.
The animals of Manor Farm have had enough. They rise up, cast out their oppressor, and build a new world on the promise that all animals are equal. But it won't last.
Van Badham's razor-sharp adaptation of Orwell's enduring fable drags the barnyard into the present tense, where the pigs have podiums, the sheep scroll and share, and the slogans change just fast enough that nobody notices. A savage, darkly comic warning that has never felt more necessary.

description:
Not Christmas, but Guy Fawkes, A theatrical double-shot from an iconic playwright and one of our greatest actors.

Bruce Mason is perhaps the most significant playwright in Aotearoa New Zealand’s theatrical history. Writing with courage and insight, he was a lover of language and a champion of the underdog.

Between 1959 and 1978, Bruce toured the country, telling uniquely Kiwi stories about emerging identity, cultural cringe and social difference. From church halls to country shearing sheds to the Edinburgh Festival, Bruce would play anywhere, in any circumstance, to any audience.

To celebrate his extraordinary legacy, Brilliant Adventures and Circa Theatre are collaborating to make two of his greatest solo works resound for a new age.

Two plays: timeless, universal, distinct. Following their critically acclaimed, sold out run of THINGS I KNOW TO BE TRUE, actor Stephen Lovatt and director Shane Bosher return to Circa for a not-to-be missed theatrical encounter with a master craftsman.


THE END OF THE GOLDEN WEATHER
“I invite you to join me, in a voyage into the past, to that territory of the heart we call childhood.”

Bruce Mason’s quintessential Kiwi classic chronicles the friendship between a 12-year-old boy and Firpo, a social outcast who dreams of winning an Olympic medal.

Through the boy’s eyes we see the wonder of life on a perfect beach, in a perfect 1930s New Zealand, during a perfect summer. It’s a world of magic and transformation, where anything can happen and miracles seem possible.

When the boy sets out to help Firpo make his athletic dream a reality, ignoring his father’s rebukes and community ridicule, a battle rages between the eternal optimism of childhood and the harsh pragmatism of adulthood.

Gliding effortlessly between flights of poetic fancy and blunt everyday speech, THE END OF THE GOLDEN WEATHER is New Zealand storytelling at its very best.


NOT CHRISTMAS, BUT GUY FAWKES
An adolescent boy tries to find his place in an adult-dominated world. A young man retraces an intensely felt boyhood experience of bullying. A playwright in his last days reconciles the value of an artistic life and challenges the idea of New Zealand identity.

Comic disasters and confronting your own hubris. NOT CHRISTMAS, BUT GUY FAWKES is a richly autobiographical search for self-expression. Profound and true, it is a set of variations about over-reaching, cheekily confronting our very own Tall Poppy Syndrome.

Celebrating Bruce Mason
Directed by Shane Bosher
Performed by Stephen Lovatt

Please note The End of the Golden Weather and Not Christmas, but Guy Fawkes tickets need to be purchases separately, see the Circa Theatre website for full dates and ticket details.

description:
Box of Birds, When: 20th – 26th September 2025
Monday - Saturday 10am
No shows on Sundays
Hailed as "the cutest little show in Aotearoa" (Hamilton Arts Festival 2024), award-winning theatre company Birdlife Productions have created this gorgeous theatre show designed especially for ages 4 to 9 years, Including exquisite puppetry, live interactive songs, projection and the teaching of a waiata, this work reflects our transformative connection to nature. Peter is reluctant to stay with nanna in the school holidays because she lives in the country and doesn't have a TV but Nanna finds ways to engage Peter in her love of the forest, especially the precious manu, when they build a nesting box for Ruru together. Peter is excited to see if Ruru will make her home in the box, waiting patiently while many other birds arrive to check out the box first! And after all that waiting, Nanna takes Peter on an exciting night time forest walk to find Ruru - in the dark! The bird characters are all familiar New Zealand locals, such as piwakawaka, kereru, tui and ruru, and the story highlights the importance of supporting them and the different needs they may have. Teachers and Parents have been ecstatic about this show and hundreds of New Zealand children have been transfixed by it.
As quoted by Theatreview: “This is truly a New Zealand show for New Zealand children and all those young-at-heart”.
